Website Development Companies help businesses improve their existing websites and enhance their functionality and performance to meet customer needs and business objectives.
A successful website depends on more than design alone. It also needs good loading speed, a clear user experience, and a technical structure that allows for future development.
Website development includes fixing technical issues, improving pages, adding features, strengthening security, and improving compatibility with search engines and different devices.

That is why successful development starts with analyzing the website and identifying what needs improvement before implementing any changes. In this article, we explore the key aspects of website development, the criteria for choosing the right company, and the main digital solutions and services offered by Nami .
The cost of website development varies depending on the type of website, project size, and required features. Below are estimated prices for developing different types of websites:
Marketing landing pages: Starting at SAR 1,500.
Corporate websites: Ranging from SAR 3,000 to SAR 18,000.
E-commerce stores: Ranging from SAR 3,500 to SAR 40,000.
Digital platforms and custom systems: Starting at SAR 25,000, and may increase depending on complexity and required functionality.

These prices are indicative. The final cost depends on each project's requirements, the degree of customization, integration with external systems, and additional services such as hosting, maintenance, and technical support.
Website development costs are affected by several factors that determine the amount of work and resources required. The most important include:
The condition of the existing website.
The number of pages and amount of content.
The type of website and nature of the business.
Required features and functionality.
Design and user experience.
Security and performance.
Search engine optimization (SEO) requirements.
Integration with external systems.
Hosting, maintenance, and technical support.
Nami provides comprehensive website development solutions at competitive prices to suit the needs of different projects.

Website development steps vary according to the nature and requirements of the project. They include several stages that help define the scope of work and organize the development process, from evaluating the website to determining the appropriate implementation plan.
Assessing the current situation: Reviewing the existing website and identifying technical issues and opportunities for improvement.
Evaluating performance and user experience: Checking page loading speed, ease of navigation, and content clarity.
Defining requirements: Identifying the functions and features needed based on the nature and goals of the business.
Setting priorities: Ranking tasks according to their importance and their impact on website performance and project goals.
Creating a development plan: Defining implementation stages, suitable solutions, and expected outcomes.

At Nami, the development process begins by understanding each project's requirements to identify solutions suited to the business and its goals, rather than relying on standardized templates that do not account for different needs. You can also benefit from technical consulting services to assess the current situation, set priorities, and choose the most suitable technical approach before implementation begins.

Website development services help businesses establish a digital presence that suits the nature of their operations, whether their goal is to showcase services, make it easier for customers to contact them, or manage operations online. These services include:
Interface design: Organizing pages to align with the company's identity and services.
User experience optimization: Making navigation and access to information easier.
Feature development: Adding features such as contact forms, booking, payments, and user registration.
Performance optimization: Increasing website speed and resolving technical issues.
Mobile compatibility: Ensuring the website works efficiently across different screen sizes.
Content management: Providing a control panel to update pages and information easily.
System integration: Connecting the website with payment services and customer relationship management systems.
Security and maintenance: Updating technical components and fixing errors to maintain website stability.

Websites that rely on changing technical resources or interconnected systems may need a scalable infrastructure. In such cases, cloud computing services may be suitable for hosting systems and managing resources, depending on the project's nature and requirements.
Your website needs development when it can no longer meet your business needs or provide an effective user experience. Common signs include:
Slow page loading and reduced website performance.
Poor mobile compatibility and difficult navigation.
Technical errors that affect website functionality.
Limited features and difficulty adding new functionality.
Difficulty managing content and updating pages.
A decline in contact requests or sales through the website.
A technical review helps identify the improvements needed and select a solution that suits the nature of your business.
You can book a consultation with Nami to assess your website's needs, identify opportunities for improvement and development, and choose technical solutions that suit your business and goals.

User experience affects visitors' ability to find information and interact with website services easily, which in turn influences conversion rates, contact requests, and sales. It can be improved through:
Organizing pages and menus to make navigation easier.
Clear headings and content to help visitors find information faster.
Simplifying contact forms and reducing the number of required steps.
Clear call-to-action buttons to encourage visitors to interact.
Improving the mobile experience to ensure ease of use across different screens.
Making services easier to access and reducing the steps needed to complete actions.

Improving user experience and having a good design help increase engagement and achieve website goals, whether attracting customers, increasing sales, or generating contact requests. Design services can help develop interfaces that align with the company's identity and make the website easier to use.

The decision depends on the condition of the current website. If its technical structure can be improved, development may be the most suitable option. However, if it has fundamental issues or cannot meet the business's requirements, building a new website may be more effective.
The appropriate next step depends on several factors:
Technical infrastructure: Whether it can be developed and expanded with new features.
Performance and technical issues: The extent of errors and their impact on website efficiency.
Required functionality: Whether the current system can support the business's needs.
Content management: How easily pages can be updated and the website managed.
Search engine optimization: Preserving important pages, links, and existing traffic when making changes.
Start by evaluating your current website with Nami to identify opportunities for improvement and determine whether updating or rebuilding it is the best option for achieving your business goals.

A website is one of the most important digital marketing tools. It helps businesses showcase their services and products, reach potential customers, and turn visits into contact requests or purchases.
To achieve the best results, website development should take several factors into account:
Search engine optimization (SEO): Improving the website's chances of appearing in search results.
User experience: Making it easier to navigate and access information and services.
Marketing content: Clarifying the services and value offered by the business.
Conversion rates: Simplifying contact and purchasing processes.
Integration with marketing channels: Supporting advertising campaigns and connecting the website with marketing and analytics tools.

Nami helps businesses develop websites that support their marketing goals. Businesses can also benefit from digital marketing services to reach their target audience more effectively and improve campaign performance.

Website development helps improve a website's search engine readiness by resolving technical issues and organizing pages and content in ways that make it easier for search engines to crawl the website and index its pages. Key aspects include:
Website speed: Improving page loading times.
Mobile compatibility: Ensuring ease of use across different screens.
Internal links: Making it easier to navigate between pages.
Headings and content: Organizing headings and improving content structure.
Crawling and indexing: Ensuring important pages can be accessed.
URL redirects: Handling moved or deleted pages to reduce access errors.
Technical errors: Identifying issues that may hinder the website's performance in search results.

For this reason, Nami takes search engine optimization (SEO) requirements into account from the website development stage by focusing on technical structure, page organization, and user experience. This supports the website's indexability and prepares it to appear in search results.
Website types vary depending on the nature of the business and its goals. The main solutions that can be developed include:
Corporate websites: Showcasing services and company information while strengthening the company's digital presence.

Website development companies in Egypt have become important partners for businesses and project owners looking to build a strong digital presence and present their services to customers professionally. A website helps showcase products and services, facilitate communication, support sales, and organize digital operations.
A website’s success depends on choosing a company with technical expertise that understands the project’s needs and can develop solutions that meet its current goals and future plans.

In this article, we explore the criteria for choosing the best website development companies in Egypt, the types of websites and digital systems available, the implementation stages, and the factors affecting cost and development time. We also look at Nami’s website development and digital solutions services and how they can help you choose the right solution for your project.

Choosing a website development company in Egypt depends on its technical expertise, quality of execution, and range of solutions. Nami is one of the distinguished companies in programming and digital solutions, combining website development, interface design, mobile applications, technical consulting, cloud services, and digital marketing to provide integrated solutions that help businesses strengthen their digital presence and achieve their goals. Discover Nami’s services and explore the solutions that can take your project to a new level of digital development.
Experience and portfolio: Review previous projects and how relevant they are to your business.
Technical expertise: Make sure the team can implement the required features and functionality.
Design quality: Choose a company that prioritizes ease of use and content organization, not just appearance.
Performance and security: Make sure the company focuses on website speed and data protection.
Clear agreements: Define the scope of work, cost, timeline, and rights related to the website.
Post-launch support: Understand the available maintenance and update services and how technical issues are handled.
Comparing these criteria helps you choose a company that suits your project’s needs and get the most value from your investment in a website.
Website types vary according to the nature of the business and the goals it aims to achieve. Therefore, the website’s primary purpose should be identified before choosing how to develop it.
The main types include:
Corporate websites: Present company information, services, and contact details, making them suitable for organizations looking to strengthen their digital presence.
E-commerce stores: Allow businesses to display products, receive orders, and manage sales and payment processes.
Service and booking websites: Help customers explore services, submit requests, or book appointments.
Digital platforms: Connect users with service providers or allow multiple operations to be managed through a single platform.
Administrative systems: Help businesses organize data and internal operations through customized functions and dashboards.
Content websites: Suit organizations that regularly publish articles, news, and educational materials.
Nami’s website development services include solutions for websites and online stores, as well as the development of interfaces and features tailored to each project’s requirements.
Defining project requirements helps you choose the right technical solution and avoid unnecessary features or repeated changes during development.
Before development begins, identify the following elements:
Website objective: Such as showcasing services, selling products, or accepting bookings.
Target audience: Identify users, their needs, and how they interact with the website.
Required pages: Such as Home, Services, About Us, and Contact.
Core functionality: Such as request forms, search, user registration, and online payments.
External integrations: Determine whether the website needs to connect with payment, shipping, or customer management systems.
Scalability: Consider the features the project may need in the future.
Budget and timeline: Define available resources and priorities before development begins.
Nami’s technical consulting services help assess project requirements and identify suitable technical solutions, supporting better planning before implementation begins.
The choice between ready-made and custom website development depends on the nature of the project, the required functionality, the available budget, and the need for future expansion.
This option suits projects that need to launch a website using an existing system or template that can be modified to meet specific requirements.
Key advantages include:
Reducing launch time in many cases.
Using ready-made features for managing content or products.
Lowering initial costs for some types of projects.
Making website management easier when using a suitable system.
However, ready-made solutions may be limited when a project requires unavailable features or complex customizations.
Custom development involves building a website or system according to the project’s specific needs rather than relying entirely on ready-made solutions. This approach suits projects that require:
Features tailored to the nature of the business.
Integration with external systems and services.
Workflows that go beyond the capabilities of ready-made solutions.
A user experience designed around the target audience’s needs.
Flexibility to add new features as the project grows.

Unlike ready-made solutions with limited capabilities, custom development offers greater flexibility in building solutions that align with business goals. This is where Nami stands out by providing digital solutions tailored to each project’s requirements, helping you turn your ideas into a practical, scalable website or system that supports business efficiency and keeps pace with your future ambitions.

The technologies used in website development affect implementation speed, scalability, ease of maintenance, and security. Therefore, technology should be selected according to project requirements, not simply because it is widely used.
Key technical components include:
Frontend: The elements visitors interact with, such as menus, buttons, and forms.
Backend: Processes data, performs functions, and connects different parts of the system.
Databases: Store, organize, and provide access to information when needed.
Application Programming Interfaces (APIs): Connect the website to other services or systems.
Security: Use encrypted connections, manage access permissions, and update software components.
Performance: Optimize file and image sizes, reduce unnecessary requests, and use caching when needed.

Websites also need suitable hosting infrastructure to ensure stable operation and scalability as a project grows. Nami’s cloud services help businesses benefit from cloud solutions that match their technical needs and the operational requirements of websites and digital systems.

Making a website compatible with phones and different devices makes browsing easier, while search engine optimization helps search engines understand the website’s content and improves its chances of appearing in relevant search results.
To achieve this, focus on the following elements:
Responsive design: Adjust pages to suit mobile phones, tablets, and computers.
Loading speed: Optimize images and files and reduce elements that affect performance.
Content organization: Use clear headings and well-structured paragraphs that are easy to read.
Link structure: Create clear links between related pages.
Metadata: Write page titles and descriptions that accurately reflect their content.
Ease of navigation: Provide clear menus and buttons that are easy to use on smaller screens.
Indexing: Ensure search engines can access important pages and that no settings unintentionally prevent them from being indexed.
User needs should also be considered when designing interfaces. Nami’s design services help create visual identities and interfaces that suit a brand’s nature and user experience requirements.
Creating a website involves several interconnected stages. Organizing these stages helps reduce errors and ensures that requirements are clear before moving to the next phase.
1. Requirements Analysis
Define the project’s goals, target audience, required pages, and functionality.
2. Website Structure Planning
Organize pages and sections and determine how users will navigate between them.
3. Interface Design
Prepare the page layouts and arrange elements to match the project’s identity and users’ needs.
4. Programming and Development
Build the interfaces and functionality, connect databases, and implement the required external services.
5. Testing and Review
Check pages, functionality, performance, and compatibility across different devices and browsers.
6. Launch
Set up the hosting, domain, and required configurations to publish the website and make it available to users.
7. Post-Launch Follow-Up
Monitor performance, resolve issues, and make necessary updates according to the project’s needs.

Nami follows a clear project management methodology that begins with defining requirements and agreeing on an implementation plan, while involving the client in key stages such as design approval and reviewing results before launch. Organized communication throughout the project helps align expectations, ensure important decisions are approved on time, and make sure the final website meets the client’s needs and business objectives.
Website testing aims to identify errors before the website becomes available to the public and ensure that pages and functions work according to the defined requirements.
The testing process covers several areas:
Functional testing: Ensure that links, forms, login, search, and ordering functions work correctly.
Device and browser testing: Verify that the website displays and functions properly across different environments.
Performance testing: Measure page loading speed and identify elements that cause delays.
Security testing: Review permissions, settings, and components that may affect data protection.
User experience testing: Ensure that content is clear and core functions are easy to access.
Integration testing: Verify that payment, shipping, or connected systems work properly when applicable.
It is best to prepare a list of requirements and tests before launch, resolve any identified issues, and retest the affected components.
Website development time varies according to the project’s size and complexity. An accurate timeline cannot be determined without understanding the requirements and functionality to be implemented.
The main factors affecting development time include:
Website size: The number of pages and sections and the amount of content required.
Level of customization: The time needed to develop custom designs and features.
External integrations: Such as payment gateways, shipping systems, and customer management tools.
Content preparation: How ready the text, images, and data are before work begins.
Decision-making speed: The time needed to review designs and approve project stages.
Testing: The number of features that need to be checked and tested before launch.
Changes during development: Modifications that fall outside the agreed scope of work.
Defining the scope of work from the beginning and establishing clear review stages help reduce delays and improve time and resource management.
The cost of website development in Egypt varies according to the website type, project size, and required features. As a general estimate, typical prices in the Egyptian market range between:
Simple landing page: EGP 5,000–15,000.
Corporate website: EGP 10,000–35,000.
E-commerce store: EGP 20,000–80,000 or more.
Custom platform or system: EGP 50,000–150,000 or more.
These prices are indicative and may vary depending on the company and project requirements. Hosting and maintenance may also be charged separately.
Website type: A corporate website has different requirements from an e-commerce store or custom platform.
Number of pages: More pages and sections may require additional design and development time.
Custom design: Creating unique interfaces may require more resources than using a ready-made template.
Software functionality: Such as user accounts, bookings, dashboards, and order management.
Integrations: Connecting the website to payment and shipping services or internal systems.
Languages: Supporting multiple languages may require preparing content and configuring interfaces and functionality for each language.
Hosting and domain: Choosing the appropriate infrastructure to run the website.
Maintenance and support: Services required after launch and their associated costs.

To obtain a suitable estimate, request a quotation that specifies the scope of work, included features, implementation timeline, and operating and maintenance costs. When comparing website development companies in Egypt, compare the actual services and quality of execution, not just the total price.
Website maintenance helps preserve stability, resolve issues, and reduce technical risks as the website continues to be used.
Essential maintenance tasks include:
Software updates: Update the content management system, plugins, and other components.
Backups: Create regular backups and test whether they can be restored.
Performance monitoring: Track website speed, resource usage, and technical errors.
Data protection: Manage user permissions and secure accounts and login credentials.
Troubleshooting: Resolve issues that affect pages or functionality.
Content updates: Modify information, services, and prices when needed.
Security reviews: Check settings, address known vulnerabilities, and apply appropriate updates.
Before signing a contract, define the scope of maintenance, support period, response time, and any additional costs to ensure the company’s responsibilities are clear after the website is delivered.
A website may need further development as a business grows and customer needs change, whether to add new services, improve performance, or simplify digital operations.
Common situations that may require website development include:
Adding new services: Updating pages and sections to reflect business expansion.
Improving user experience: Making navigation and access to information and services easier.
Adding new features: Such as bookings, account management, and order tracking.
System integration: Connecting the website with customer management or inventory systems.
Improving performance: Handling an increase in visitors and orders efficiently.

Designing a mobile app has become an important step for companies that want to deliver their services more easily, reach customers, and develop new revenue streams. However, an app’s success depends on more than programming alone; it starts with a clear idea, a suitable business model, and features that meet users’ needs.

If you are looking for mobile app design companies in Jeddah , it is important to know how to choose the right company, what to define before starting the project, and how to plan the app’s cost and expected return.
In this article, we explore the key decisions that can help turn an app idea into a scalable digital project, while introducing Nami’s mobile app design and development solutions.

An app design company does more than build screens and implement requested features. Its role also includes understanding the project idea and turning it into a digital experience that can be used and developed over time.
A company’s tasks typically include:
Idea analysis: Identifying the problem the app addresses and its target audience.
Feature definition: Selecting the core functions users need.
Interface design: Organizing screens and making services easy to access.
Software development: Building the app and connecting its functions and databases.
Testing: Ensuring features work correctly before launch.
Publication preparation: Preparing the app and its technical requirements for submission to the appropriate stores.

Nami is one of the leading providers of mobile app development services , turning ideas into innovative apps that combine professional design with strong performance to meet the needs of the Saudi market and help businesses strengthen their digital presence and achieve their commercial goals.
Before design and programming begin, you need to define how the app will deliver value to users and how the business will benefit from operating it.
Start by answering these questions:
What problem does the app solve? Does it save time, simplify purchases, organize bookings, or improve service delivery?
Who is the target user? Individuals, businesses, service providers, or a specific customer segment?
What is the current alternative? Do customers rely on a website, phone calls, or manual processes?
What will make the app useful? Identify a practical benefit that encourages users to choose it and return to it.
How will you measure success? Define measurable outcomes, such as completed orders, subscriptions, or active users.

This process helps you avoid developing features your audience does not need and direct your budget toward functions that deliver real value. Nami’s technical consulting services can help you assess project requirements and choose suitable technical solutions before implementation begins.
The right revenue model depends on the type of app, its audience, and the value it provides. Common models include:
This model suits e-commerce stores and apps that offer paid products or services. Revenue depends on sales, profit margins, order fulfillment costs, and customer acquisition costs.

This model can be used by apps that provide ongoing content or services in exchange for a monthly or annual subscription. It requires continuously delivering value that encourages users to stay subscribed.
This model suits apps that connect customers with service providers. The app earns a commission for each completed order or booking, according to the agreed business model.
Apps with a suitable user base can generate revenue through advertising or by selling additional features within the app, provided these methods do not negatively affect the user experience.
How do you choose the right model?
Identify whether your audience is willing to pay.
Calculate operating and user acquisition costs.
Compare expected revenue with ongoing expenses.
Test the model on a limited scale before expanding.
Review results and adjust the revenue approach when necessary.

Nami can help you develop a mobile app aligned with your business goals through carefully planned technical solutions that support a distinctive user experience and prepare your app to grow and benefit from revenue opportunities.

The required features vary according to the business and target audience. It is therefore best to focus on functions that make the app easier to use and support real business operations, rather than adding features without a clear need.
Features that may be useful for apps targeting the Saudi market include:
Arabic interface: Correctly supporting right-to-left (RTL) text direction.
Suitable payment options: Based on the business and the payment methods supported by the service provider.
Order and booking management: Tracking transactions and reducing errors.
Notifications: Informing users about important order updates, appointments, and offers.
Location services: When delivery or location-based services are needed.
Account and permission management: Protecting user data and controlling access to app functions.
Easy communication: Providing a clear channel for inquiries and support.
Device compatibility: Testing the app on the devices and operating system versions it targets.
These features should be selected according to the project. A commercial app does not necessarily need the same functions as a booking app or a field-service app.
Arabic apps require attention to interface details, not just translating text from one language to another. The way menus, buttons, numbers, and forms are displayed affects clarity and ease of use.
To improve the experience for Arabic-speaking users, consider the following:
Interface direction: Arrange elements to suit right-to-left text.
Clear wording: Use direct, easy-to-understand language.
Number and date formats: Choose formats appropriate for the app and its audience.
Simple forms: Organize registration fields, addresses, and contact details.
Relevant content: Use examples and information suited to the target market.
Real interface testing: Ensure elements do not overlap or appear in the wrong direction.
Nami’s design services can help create interfaces that match the project’s identity and users’ needs, with a focus on clear layouts and easy interaction.
A project may begin with a simple mobile app idea, but additional components may be needed to support efficient operations as the business grows.
For example, a project may include:
Customer app: For browsing services or products and placing orders.
Service provider or driver app: For receiving tasks and updating their status when needed.
Admin dashboard: For managing users, orders, content, and reports.
Backend and database: For processing, storing, and organizing information.
Website: For presenting information or providing services that complement the app. Nami’s website development services can help build websites suited to the project and its digital needs.
External integrations: Such as payment, shipping, or customer management systems.
You do not need to build all these components from the start. You can launch an initial version with core features, then add other components according to project needs and usage results.
One important technical decision is how to build the app, as this affects cost, maintenance, performance, and future development.
Native Development:
Build a separate app for each operating system.
Access system capabilities directly.
Suitable for projects that require specialized features or deep device integration.
May require more resources to develop and maintain apps for both systems.
Cross-Platform Development:
Use a technology that allows much of the code to be shared between Android and iOS.
Can reduce duplicated work in some projects.
Suitable for many apps that need to run on both systems.
May require additional solutions for certain specialized features.
Neither approach is best for every app. The choice depends on required functions, performance needs, budget, and the future development plan.
A clear contract helps organize the relationship between the client and the development company and prevent disputes over features, costs, and delivery.
Before signing, make sure the following points are clear:
Scope of work: The functions, screens, and systems included in the project.
Delivery stages: Expected deliverables at each stage.
Timeline: Estimated duration and conditions for changing it if requirements change.
Cost: Project price, payment terms, and potential additional costs.
Revisions: Number of review rounds and how change requests will be handled.
Ownership rights: Ownership of code, design, files, and accounts after handover.
Testing and acceptance: Criteria for approving the app before launch.
Maintenance and support: Support period, scope, and cost of additional services.
Confidentiality and data: Each party’s responsibilities regarding information and data used.
It is best to document any change in scope after work begins and clarify its impact on cost and timeline before approving it.
Finishing the programming does not mean the app is immediately ready for publication. Each store has requirements related to quality, privacy, content, and how the app is presented to users.
Before submission, review the following:
Ensure all functions are complete and there are no critical errors.
Test the app on the targeted devices and operating system versions.
Prepare the app name, description, icon, and screenshots.
Create a clear privacy policy that matches the data the app collects.
Review the permissions requested by the app and ensure they are necessary.
Provide test credentials if the app includes sign-in or restricted features.
Ensure links and support information work correctly.
Review the relevant store’s policies before submitting the app.

Apple’s App Review Guidelines highlight the importance of app completeness, reliable functionality, and clear information before review. You should also check current Google Play requirements based on the app type and features.

The cost of building a mobile app in Jeddah varies according to project size, required features, development approach, and the systems the app needs to connect to. Therefore, the scope of work should be defined before confirming the final price.
As a general guide, costs may fall into the following ranges:
Simple app: May start at around SAR 10,000 if its functions are limited.
Mid-range app: May cost between SAR 20,000 and SAR 50,000, depending on its requirements.
Advanced app: May cost SAR 60,000–120,000 or more when multiple features and integrations are needed.

These are general estimates, not actual quotations, and costs can vary significantly from one project to another. Prices should be confirmed with the development company based on the actual requirements.
The initial budget may include:
Idea analysis and scope definition.
Interface and user experience design.
Programming and feature development.
Admin dashboard and connected systems.
Testing and bug fixing.
Preparing app files for publication.
The budget does not end when the app is delivered. The project may have ongoing expenses, including:
Hosting and cloud services.
Fees for accounts or external services, where applicable.
Maintenance and updates.
Performance monitoring and troubleshooting.
Development of new features.
Marketing and user acquisition.
Nami’s cloud services help businesses use cloud solutions suited to the operation of digital systems, based on project requirements and the technical infrastructure in use.
For a realistic estimate, request a quotation that separates development costs from operating and maintenance expenses and identifies features that can be postponed to later phases.

You can reduce the risk of investing in an unsuitable idea by testing it before building the full app. The goal is to confirm that the audience has a real need and determine whether the proposed solution offers value worth using or paying for.
Follow these steps:
Talk to potential customers: Ask about the problem they face and how they currently deal with it.
Analyze existing alternatives: Review competing apps and identify what they offer and what they lack.
Define the minimum features: Select the essential functions needed to test the idea.
Create a prototype: Present the proposed screens and user journey before full development.
Test with users: Observe how clearly they understand the idea and how easily they complete key tasks.
Review the results: Adjust features or the business model based on feedback.
Develop gradually: Add other functions as the need becomes clear.
This approach helps identify problems early and direct resources toward the most important features instead of spending the budget on functions whose value has not been validated.

After launch, you need to monitor usage data to determine whether the app is delivering the desired results. Choose metrics based on the project’s main objective rather than relying on download numbers alone.
Key metrics include:
Active users: The number of people using the app during a defined period.
Order completion rate: The percentage of users who complete a purchase or booking.
User retention rate: Whether users return to the app.
Conversion rate: The percentage of users who complete the desired action.
Average order value: An important metric for sales-based apps.
Crash rate: A measure of app stability and issues that affect usage.
User ratings: A way to identify weaknesses and opportunities for improvement.
Regularly reviewing this data helps set priorities. The solution may be to simplify registration, improve app speed, or change how services are presented—not necessarily to add new features.

The success of a project depends on choosing a development company that understands the nature of the business, accurately defines technical requirements, and selects the appropriate software architecture rather than simply building a website that does not meet actual business needs.

Criteria for Choosing a Website Development Company in Saudi Arabia That Fits Your Business

Choosing a website development company in Saudi Arabia should not depend solely on price or the website's final appearance. It also requires evaluating the company's ability to understand project requirements and turn them into a practical, scalable technical solution.
The key criteria to consider include:
Understanding the Business: The company should be able to identify the processes your website needs to support, whether that involves receiving orders, managing bookings, or presenting services.
Technical Expertise: Evaluate the team's experience in developing websites, systems, and the specific features your project requires.
Portfolio: Review previous projects to understand the types of solutions the company has delivered and how relevant they are to your requirements.
Clear Scope of Work: Ensure that the required features and expected deliverables are defined before development begins.
Scalability: Choose a solution that allows new features to be added and other systems to be integrated as your business grows.
Post-Launch Support: Agree in advance on the scope of maintenance, updates, and troubleshooting services.

It is also important to choose a company that can discuss technical alternatives and explain the advantages and costs of each option, helping you make a decision that suits your budget and future plans.
Nami's website development services provide businesses with websites and web solutions tailored to their operations and digital requirements.

Choosing between a ready-made website and one built through custom development affects how the website is managed, how easily it can be developed further, and its overall long-term cost. There is no single option that suits every business; the right choice depends on the project's size and required features.

These websites rely on pre-built templates or systems that can be customized within their available capabilities. They may be suitable for projects that need to launch a website with common features and a limited budget.
Their main advantages include:
Reducing the time required to launch the website in many cases.
Taking advantage of ready-made plugins and features.
Managing content through established platforms.
Lowering initial costs for some projects.
However, limitations may arise when a business requires features that are unavailable in the system or substantial changes to how it operates.
Custom-developed websites are built according to project requirements, with features and technical architecture designed to suit the business and the operations the website needs to perform.
Their main advantages include:
Feature Customization: Designing functionality that meets actual business needs.
Integration with Other Systems: Connecting the website to external services and systems according to project requirements.
Control Over Processes and Data: Organizing data processing to suit the nature of the business.
Flexibility and Scalability: Modifying the website and adding new features as the business grows.

Nami adopts the Custom Development approach to build websites and software solutions tailored to each project's needs, supported by Nami's integrated digital services . This approach makes it possible to develop features that suit the business while maintaining the flexibility to modify and expand the solution in the future.
The best choice is the solution that meets your project's current needs and provides the flexibility to develop it without unnecessary technical limitations.

A traditional website is suitable when the main goal is to present company information, services, and contact details. However, some businesses require functionality beyond displaying content, making a custom web system a more suitable option.
Situations that may require a custom system include:
Order Management: When a business needs to record orders, track their status, and update their details.
Customer Portals: When customers need personal accounts to access their information, documents, or orders.
Booking Systems: When a service requires appointment scheduling, availability management, and confirmation notifications.
Internal Operations Management: When employees need different access permissions and defined workflows.
Data Management and Reporting: When a business needs to collect and analyze information and generate operational reports.
Multi-Party Services: When a system connects customers, service providers, and administrators through a single platform.

Before development begins, it is important to define the processes the system will handle, the users who will interact with it, the data it needs to store, and the permissions required for each user group.

Nami's technical consulting services help assess project requirements and evaluate potential solutions before defining the development scope, supporting the selection of an architecture suited to business needs.

A website may need to exchange data with other systems to ensure that business operations work together seamlessly. Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) are used to organize communication between systems according to the rules supported by each system.
Examples of integrations include:
Online Payment Gateways: Enabling customers to complete payments and track transaction results.
Customer Relationship Management Systems (CRM): Transferring customer data and organizing follow-up activities.
Shipping and Delivery Systems: Exchanging order information and updating shipping details when the required integration is available.
Inventory Systems: Synchronizing product and stock data between the website and internal systems.
Accounting Systems: Exchanging transaction and invoice data according to the available capabilities.
Messaging and Notification Services: Sending alerts related to orders or other actions.

Connecting systems helps reduce manual data entry, minimize duplicate information, and improve operational tracking. However, successful integration requires checking system compatibility, ensuring that the necessary APIs are available, defining permissions, and establishing error-handling procedures.
When a project requires a mobile app that integrates with its website, Nami's mobile app development services can help assess an appropriate solution based on project requirements.
Technical planning should also document connected systems, the data being exchanged, connection security measures, and responsibilities for maintaining integrations when any system is updated.

A control panel gives teams an administrative interface for managing website features and monitoring operations, eliminating the need to modify code every time information needs to be updated or a recurring task needs to be performed.
Depending on the website's purpose, a control panel may include:
Content Management: Editing published pages, articles, images, and information.
User Management: Creating and updating accounts and organizing access permissions.
Order Management: Reviewing orders, updating their status, and tracking their details.
Product and Service Management: Updating prices, descriptions, and availability when needed.
Reports and Analytics: Displaying data that helps management monitor business activity.
Activity Logs: Recording certain administrative actions to support review and auditing.
It is important not to grant all users the same permissions. Organizing roles helps prevent unnecessary access to sensitive data and functions.

Administrative features should also be designed around everyday workflows. A good control panel is not necessarily the most complex one, but rather the one that enables teams to perform their tasks clearly and efficiently. Alongside the technical structure, Nami's design services can help create user interfaces that suit the project and its users' needs.
Databases and software architecture are essential foundations of website development because they determine how information is stored and processed and how different functions are connected.
Choosing the right architecture depends on several factors, including:
Nature of the Data: The type of information the website needs to store and process.
Expected Usage Volume: The number of users and operations handled by the system.
Functional Complexity: The number of systems and functions that need to be integrated.
Security Requirements: Protecting data and organizing access permissions.
Scalability: The ability to add new features in the future.
Ease of Maintenance: Organizing and documenting code to simplify updates and troubleshooting.

Technologies such as MySQL and PostgreSQL are used to manage databases, while technologies such as Laravel and Node.js are used in website development. The choice depends on the project's nature and requirements.

It is also important to organize the code, document the system architecture, and establish backup and data recovery procedures to simplify maintenance and reduce future technical issues. Alongside the software architecture, Nami's design services help create user interfaces (UI) and improve the user experience (UX), making websites easier to use and better aligned with visitors' needs.

Ownership rights and access to files and accounts are important matters to agree on before contracting a website development company. Receiving a website does not necessarily mean that all files, accounts, and permissions have automatically been transferred to the client.
Therefore, make sure the following points are clearly defined in the contract:
Source Code: Specify whether source code delivery is included in the agreement and what rights the client has to use and modify it.
Design Files and Documentation: Define the files to be delivered, including system documentation and configuration details.
Hosting and Domain Accounts: Clarify account ownership and how administrative access will be transferred.
Control Panel: Provide the administrative credentials and permissions needed to manage the website.
Third-Party Licenses: Identify licenses for templates, libraries, or paid services used by the website.
Technical Documentation: Provide the essential information needed to understand, operate, and maintain the system.
Post-Delivery Support: Specify the support period, included services, and any additional costs.
These terms should be documented clearly in the contract, including each party's responsibilities for backups, updates, and account security.

Prior agreement helps prevent disputes and gives the business owner greater clarity when managing and developing the website in the future. Nami works to clarify project requirements and delivery scope before development begins, helping clients understand their rights and responsibilities regarding the website, files, and software systems.

Not every old website requires a complete rebuild; in some cases, partial updates may be sufficient. However, continuing to rely on a system that no longer meets business needs can increase maintenance costs and make it more difficult to add new features.
Signs that your existing website may need a technical assessment include:
Difficulty adding new features or modifying existing ones.
Dependence on technologies or plugins that are no longer supported.
Recurring errors or difficulty identifying their causes.
Inability to integrate with systems required by the business.
High maintenance costs compared with the value of possible improvements.
Limitations in data management or user permissions.
Missing technical documentation or code that is difficult to understand.

Before deciding to rebuild the website, it is best to conduct a technical assessment of the existing system, identify which features are working well, determine which issues need to be addressed, and establish which data must be preserved during the transition.

The right solution may involve updating certain components, rebuilding specific sections, or developing an entirely new system. The decision depends on the website's condition, the cost of each option, and the risks associated with the transition.

E-commerce Store: Approximately SAR 10,000–40,000, depending on features and integrations.
Custom Platform or Web System: May start at SAR 20,000–40,000 and exceed this range for large projects.

These figures are estimates, not binding quotations. Actual prices may vary depending on project requirements, the development company, and the technologies used. A website design company in Jeddah is one of the key services businesses need to strengthen their digital presence and reach potential customers, especially as users increasingly rely on search engines to find services and compare companies before making a purchase decision.

Professional website design is not limited to an attractive appearance. It also includes code quality, loading speed, ease of use, and content organization according to search engine optimization (SEO) standards, helping search engines understand website pages and supporting their chances of appearing in Google search results.

That is why Nami Tec provides website design and development solutions that combine professional design with technical requirements, tailored to the nature and goals of different businesses, and helping build well-organized websites that can be developed over time.

Creating a successful website requires combining design, development, and search engine optimization so that these elements work together to provide visitors with a complete experience. Good planning before implementation helps determine the required pages, organize content, and choose the functions a business needs.
When looking for the best website design company in Jeddah, it is important to make sure it pays attention to elements such as:
Designing clear, easy-to-use interfaces.
Developing a website that works across mobile phones and different devices.
Organizing website pages to make navigation between them easier.
Considering loading speed and technical performance.
Making it easy to manage content and update pages.
Preparing the website technically for crawling and indexing.

Nami Tec’s website design and development services help businesses choose digital solutions that suit their project requirements. SEO needs should also be defined within the project scope before implementation begins.

Preparing a website for search engines starts with how it is built and how its pages are organized, not with adding keywords after the design is complete. The clearer and better organized the pages are, the easier it is for users to find information and for search engines to understand the content.
The most important standards for SEO-friendly website design include:
Clear page structure: Dividing the website into sections and connected pages according to the services offered.
Organized headings: Using a main heading and subheadings that reflect the topic of each page.
Readable URLs: Choosing clear URL addresses that suit the content.
Responsive design: Ensuring the website is easy to use on screens of different sizes.
Readable content: Presenting information in clear paragraphs and lists when needed.
Scalability: Providing a structure that allows new pages and services to be added without disrupting the existing organization.
These standards help create a website that is easier to use and manage, while providing a suitable foundation for ongoing search engine optimization.

Development affects search engines’ ability to access website pages, read their content, and index them. Therefore, website development should go beyond implementing the required functions to include checking that essential pages work properly and that important content can be discovered.
The aspects that should be considered during website development include:
Ensuring important pages can be accessed without technical barriers.
Avoiding unnecessary duplicate pages.
Reviewing internal links and ensuring they work.
Using appropriate redirects when page URLs change.
Ensuring the main content is accessible to search engines.
Testing functions, forms, and links before launching the website.

Design and development alone do not guarantee a specific Google ranking. Visibility depends on multiple factors, including content quality, relevance to search intent, competition, and the website’s technical performance.

User interface (UI) design and user experience (UX) help make a website clearer and easier to use. When visitors can find the service they need without complicated steps, their experience improves, increasing the chances that they will interact with the website and complete the required actions.
To improve the user experience on a website, attention should be given to the following:
Placing main menus in clear, visible locations.
Using fonts and colors that make content easier to read.
Arranging information according to its importance to visitors.
Making contact and service-request buttons clear.
Reducing the steps required to submit forms.
Providing a clear path between services and related pages.
Nami Tec is committed to providing design solutions that combine a professional appearance with ease of use by developing digital interfaces that consider user needs and the nature of each project.
You can explore Nami Tec’s design services to create interfaces that present content clearly, enhance the visitor experience, and support your business’s digital goals.

Mobile compatibility and page loading speed are important elements of professional website design, as they help visitors browse content and access services easily. Improving performance and usability also supports SEO efforts, especially because Google uses the mobile version of a website for indexing.
Image compression: Reducing file sizes while maintaining image quality.
Code optimization: Reducing unnecessary files and improving how they load.
Server performance optimization: Reducing response time so pages load efficiently.
Website testing: Reviewing performance on mobile phones, computers, and different networks.
Browsing experience improvements: Ensuring text and buttons are clear and menus and forms are easy to use.

Core Web Vitals help evaluate how quickly content appears, how quickly a page responds to user interactions, and how stable page elements remain during loading. Therefore, a website should be tested and issues identified by performance measurement tools should be addressed, rather than relying on visual impressions alone.

Nami Tec focuses on developing web solutions that suit each project and its users’ needs. You can explore examples of its work, such as the Across the East Recruitment website and the Steel Beams website , along with other Nami Tec projects, to learn about the range of digital solutions the company offers.

Keywords help identify the topics a website’s pages should target, while internal links make it easier to navigate between related pages. Both should be organized to serve users’ needs rather than repeating keywords or adding unnecessary links.
Choose a suitable primary keyword for each page.
Use the keyword naturally in the page title.
Write a meta description that explains the page content and encourages users to visit.
Organize content using clear subheadings.
Add internal links to related services or articles.
Optimize images with descriptive file names and suitable alt text.
Review similar pages to avoid overlap in keyword targeting.
For example, a service page should target a phrase related to the service itself, while articles can focus on informational topics and questions customers search for.

Each internal link should have a clear purpose, such as directing visitors to details about a service or a relevant work example, and its anchor text should explain the content of the destination page.

Technical SEO helps prepare a website so search engines can discover, understand, and index important pages. Some incorrect settings may affect page visibility even when the content is relevant to the audience.
The main elements of a technical review include:
XML Sitemap: Helps provide search engines with a list of important page URLs.
Robots.txt file: Defines crawling rules; ensure that pages meant to be discovered are not blocked.
Indexing settings: Review directives such as Noindex on pages intended to appear in search results.
404 errors: Fix links that lead to pages that do not exist when an appropriate destination is available.
Redirects: Direct users and search engines to the correct URL when pages are moved.
Structured data: Use it when suitable for the page content, while ensuring the information is accurate and meets the requirements of the relevant type.
Nami Tec reviews websites before launch to check link functionality, indexing settings, and whether search engines can access important pages.

This review helps identify and address technical issues early, rather than discovering them after launch when they may affect the website’s readiness for search engines. As a result, clients receive a technically reviewed website with a stronger foundation for SEO efforts and improved visibility in Google search results.

Local search engine optimization helps businesses improve their chances of appearing to people searching for services in Jeddah. This involves providing accurate information about the business and its service area, as well as preparing website pages to address local search queries.
Key local SEO practices include:
Clarifying the service area and geographic location when appropriate.
Creating local pages that provide genuine information about the available services.
Keeping the business name, contact details, and address consistent across different platforms.
Setting up and managing a Google Business Profile if the business is eligible.
Providing clear information about services and contact methods.
Monitoring search queries that attract visitors from the target area.

Applying local SEO strategies as part of website design can therefore improve a company’s chances of appearing in search results related to its services in Jeddah, making it easier for potential customers to find its services and contact information.

Service pages play an important role in the customer journey because they explain what a company offers and help visitors determine whether a service meets their needs. For this reason, a page should combine clear content, ease of use, and a direct way to get in touch.
An effective service page includes the following elements:
A clear title describing the main service.
A brief explanation of the scope of work and the benefits offered.
Details that answer customers’ important questions.
Subheadings that organize the information.
Examples of previous work, when available.
A clear button to request a quote or get in touch.
Links to related services or information.

When comparing website design companies, the decision should not be based on the final appearance or price alone. Choosing the right company requires checking implementation quality, a clearly defined scope of work, and the ability to manage and develop the website after delivery.
Key criteria to review include:
Previous work: Review completed projects and make sure they suit the nature of your business.
Design quality: Ensure ease of use and compatibility with different devices.

Content management: Check whether text, headings, and meta descriptions can be edited.
Technical support: Find out what support and maintenance are included after delivery.

Clear deliverables: Agree on the required functions, delivery date, and each party’s responsibilities.
These criteria help you evaluate proposals more accurately and choose a company that can meet current project requirements while taking future development needs into account.
